newsitem.title: USA: U.S. defense chief to visit Nordic countries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. defense chief to visit Nordic countries.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry will visit Finland, Sweden, Denmark and Norway Sept. 21-29 on a trip that will include talks on Bosnia with defence leaders of NATO and Russia, the Pentagon said on Tuesday.
The centrepiece of the trip will be an annual informal gathering of Atlantic alliance defence ministers in Bergen, Norway, on Wednesday and Thursday of next week to discuss Bosnia and other issues.

Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodinov will attend a special session at the NATO meeting and sign an agreement with Perry and Norway's Defence Minister Joergen Kosmo under which the three nations will cooperate to clean up nuclear and other waste dumped by Russia's military in the vast Arctic.

U.S. defence officials, who asked not to be identified, said the NATO ministers would not reach any decision on whether U.S. and other international troops will remain in Bosnia next year, but that the issue would be discussed.
A decision on whether the Western allies, Russia and other countries will send troops for any new peacekeeping mission in Bosnia is unlikely to come until at least December, the officials said.

A senior defence official said Perry looked forward to private talks with Rodinov on continued U.S. bilateral and other cooperation with Russia, which grew out of close ties between Perry and former Russian Defence Minister Pavel Grachev.
Grachev was sacked by Russian President Boris Yeltsen this summer in a domestic shakeup over the military's handling of the bloody civil war in Chechnya.

"The secretary (Perry), I think, is looking forward very much to building on the progress in defence cooperation, both bilaterally and multilaterally, that he had achieved with Minister Grachev earlier," the official said.

The Perry-Rodinov talks will include "the general state of NATO-Russia relations, the continuation of Russian cooperation within IFOR (Bosnia peace implementation force) and development of an expanded scope for bilateral military programmes and other activities involving Russia and the United States," the official added.
Before the NATO meeting, Perry will visit Helsinki on Saturday followed by Stockholm on Sunday and Copenhagen on Monday for bilateral talks with government and defence leaders.

In Copenhagen on Tuesday morning, he will take part in a Baltic defence seminar hosted by Danish Defence Minister Has Haekkerup and including Defence Ministers Michael Portillo of Britain, Volker Ruehe of Germany and others, U.S. officials said.
